title: Book Group: From Dawn to Decadence
contentHtml:
Twenty-six years ago a ninety-two-year-old scholar had a best-selling book about Western intellectual thought — From Dawn to Decadence by Jacques Barzun.

It was a surprising hit given its subject, length (800 pages), and depth. Intrigued, I recently picked it up and quickly understood why — it’s a remarkably easy and enjoyable read, despite its density. His style is conversational, warm, and smooth, and it feels like having tea with an especially erudite, eccentric, and insightful professor emeritus.

It’s a book I want to read carefully because while I might not always agree with it, I’m sure I’ll come away knowing more. That’s the perfect book for a group read, because the weekly discussions provide the discipline to plow through it all, while helping to flesh out our thoughts.

So I figured, why not do it with some of you, via Zoom!

It will take us eighteen weeks, with weekly readings of about fifty pages, and then an hour and a half of discussion one evening a week (Right now, Monday at 8 p.m. seems best).
